processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm; plates then cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining.
Samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
The solution-treated sample was aged at 650 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching. This is the terminal state characterized by EBSD in Fig. 4(c).

structures.overall_structure: For the 15Al (Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu) alloy aged at 650 °C for 3 h, the untransformed α regions were no longer observed and a new FCC phase was distributed in β-Mn, i.e. the α matrix had fully transformed so that β-Mn is the dominant (matrix) phase. The combined volume fraction of the FCC Cu-rich and BCC phases between the β-Mn interfaces was 3.9 % for this condition.

phases_present.morphology: fine particles at the β-Mn interfaces

interfaces.phase_evolution: For the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels the aging microstructure evolution followed the sequence α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase. For this sample (15Al, 650 °C/3 h) the α matrix had fully transformed: untransformed α was no longer observed and a new FCC phase was distributed in β-Mn.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness: load 9.8 N for 15 s, 5 repeated measurements averaged; electrolytically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol) before characterization.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the value given by the average of 5 measurements; specimens electrolytically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the aged 15Al samples after the different aging treatments.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 15Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 3 h showed a Vickers hardness of 852.3 ± 13.8 HV; hardness at 650 °C stabilized between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification observations
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol).
characterization_methods.purpose: Clarify the microstructural origin of the rapid aging hardening by identifying constituent phases of the 15Al alloy after different aging treatments.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For 15Al aged at 650 °C for 3 h (Fig. 4c), the untransformed α regions were no longer observed; the phase map is dominated by β-Mn with sparse FCC specks, and the magnified view shows scattered particles labelled 'New FCC phase' within the β-Mn matrix.

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy, the optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness was mainly 525-600 °C, based on the hardness contour plots (Fig. 2a); this is an alloy-level (not 650 °C/3 h-specific) finding.

The ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g reported for the Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu (15Al) alloy corresponds to its peak-hardness state (965.6 HV, 600 °C/6 h), not to the 650 °C/3 h aging state of this sample, whose hardness is 852.3 HV.

In the EBSD phase map of the 15Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 3 h (Fig. 4c2), the magnified map's base colour is red/salmon (the colour used for BCC/α elsewhere in the figure) while the caption identifies that matrix as β-Mn; the scattered magenta particles are labelled 'New FCC phase'.
At 650 °C the 15Al hardness decreased monotonically with aging time from 857.1 ± 15.4 HV (1 h) to 842.3 ± 3.7 HV (10 h); the 3 h value of 852.3 ± 13.8 HV lies within this plateau.
